display.title: Chazak, Chazak: Finishing Vayikra and Beginning Chumash Bamidbar
display.summary_short: Why we speak softly in shul, why everyone calls out 'Chazak, chazak' when a Chumash is finished, and the joy of beginning Bamidbar.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given the week after the reading of Vayikra was completed. Uncle Yossi explains that the shul is a Beis HaKnesses, Hashem's own house, so we never shout there and always speak softly. Yet last Shabbos everyone called out at the top of their voices, 'Chazak, chazak, v'nischazek!' as the Baal Korei read the last verse of the third Chumash. That burst of joy means that our strength comes from the Torah: Torah is our strength and our life. He reviews the five books of the Torah, Bereishis, Shemos, Vayikra, Bamidbar and Devarim, and invites children to be in shul this Shabbos to hear the start of Bamidbar, the fourth book, and to thank Hashem for letting us keep learning His Torah.
display.lesson: The shul is Hashem's house, so we behave there with respect; and the Torah is our strength, so we rejoice each time we finish a book and begin the next.
